reportedFacts: The public issue triage workflow let non-write users invoke a Claude action with Bash access on the default branch.
The triage run shared the default-branch cache scope with nightly publication workflows that restored node_modules.
Cline's postmortem reports that an attacker obtained a still-active npm publishing token and published cline@2.3.0 without authorization on February 17, 2026.
The unauthorized package added a postinstall command to install OpenClaw; the maintainers report that the CLI binary was otherwise unchanged and no malicious code was delivered.
The February 9 mitigation removed AI triage workflows and publication-workflow cache use.
